# FDG8012

> DO seal custom attribute classes, if possible. This makes the look-up for the attribute faster.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.2 Attributes.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (full coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1813
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: verified

CA1813 reports every attribute class that is neither abstract nor sealed, public or internal (probe with SDK 10.0.402), including one that other attributes derive from. The text says "if possible": an attribute that is meant to be a base class is a reason to keep it unsealed, and such a report can be suppressed. The SDK code fix seals the class (probe), and sealing a public class stops callers from deriving from it, which changes the public API, so the fix is breaking.

## From the book

```csharp
public sealed class NameAttribute : Attribute { ... }
```

> **Jason Clark:** In the exception section, I cautioned against the reuse of somebody else’s exception type. Here I am going to do the same for custom attributes. Reuse of somebody else’s custom attribute, unless it means exactly the same thing, puts your mutual clients in the awkward position of having to choose between avoiding your API and applying the co-opted attribute, which involves the risk of unexpected or expected (but undesirable) side effects from the original code that used the attribute.
